cards.viewer_question: Why were valuable goods brought to mainland quarantine despite deaths aboard?
cards.promise: Trade, warning signs and quarantine decisions.
cards.title: They Brought the Cargo Ashore. Plague Followed.
cards.visual: An official hesitates over a clearance ledger beside an open silk bale inside the Lazaret. No ship.
cards.film_basis: Accepted transcript: valuable textiles, Beaucaire deadline, trade connections, deaths aboard, mainland Lazaret decision; precise transmission remains uncertain.

cards.viewer_question: What happened to daily life when Marseille was cut off by epidemic?
cards.promise: Life in a trading city whose hospitals and ordinary services were overwhelmed.
cards.title: Marseille 1720: Life Inside a City Cut Off by Plague
cards.visual: Traveler faces a blocked street, guards and shuttered market. No cargo, ships or prison.
cards.film_basis: Accepted transcript: hospitals filled, attempted flight, restrictions, interrupted trade and burial crisis.

cards.viewer_question: Why was the captain freed after a catastrophic voyage and the destruction of his ship?
cards.promise: The captain’s arrest, nearly three years in custody and the case dismissed in 1723.
cards.title: His Ship Burned. Why Was the Captain Set Free?
cards.visual: Close-up of a merchant captain behind prison bars in a stone island cell. No ship, goods or street.
cards.film_basis: Accepted transcript: ship burned near Jarre; Chataud imprisoned at Château d’If; released by court order in 1723. No assertion of deliberate infection or sole responsibility.
